comments.body: https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/844

When creating a "binary" resource in the HTML UI, nothing is shown on the landing page.

I am also seeing this unwanted triple when requesting:
GET http://localhost:8080/rest/book/page/fcr:metadata
...
fedora:hasVersions <http://localhost:8080/rest/book/page/jcr:content/fcr:versions>
...
Note: 'jcr:content'

"jcr:content"!

I will examine this at the top of the week.
What is supposed to be shown for a binary resource? I thought it would go right to the bitstream.
If you are talking about the HTML UI, both GET requests to the binary redirect to the description, which shows the properties.
Wait, so a GET request for the bitstream gives you the HTML display of the metadata? That doesn't sound right.
Give the HTML UI a look, it will make more sense. There is also a "Download" button for getting the content itself.
Do we have a demo site up somewhere?
No, but the "one-click run" you established works nicely.
What happened to the demo site that Oxford ran?
They dropped support... Ladd at Texas is standing up a new one as we speak.
Oh, that's nice of Hanson, Ladd. Are they using Fedora?
Hanson, Ladd can speak for himself... but I believe some of their services are moving in that direction.
No, using a "stock" Fedora, when I go to the URI of a bitstream in the HTML view, I get what I would expect: the bitstream. Not properties.
you mean the bitstream downloads??
Yes, of course. If I make a bitstream at uri and point my browser at uri the bitstream downloads, which is just what I expect and want. Why would I want to be redirected to a properties page?
For me, if I put the binary uri in the browser, it downloads. However, if I navigate to the binary, I am redirected to the description.
Navigate from what page?
hope to have the demo site up in the next day or so. Yes! we have big plans for Fedora. <smile>
A. Soroka, navigate in the HTML from anywhere in the repository... say for example, from the root resource.
When I do that, I get the properties page you describe as being the expected result.

With PR: https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/844
That properties page renders empty.
Why is that link going to the properties page at all? That seems totally wrong to me.

Because the notion of "describedby" [1] defined in the LDP maps nicely onto what a UI user would likely want to see when navigating in the HTML UI to a NonRdfSource, i.e. a description of that resource.
It is a very annoying user experience to be navigating in the HTML UI and constantly, and unintentionally, hitting resource downloads.

[1] http://www.w3.org/TR/ldp/#link-relation-describedby

That's not my point: I don't care what links are provided in the UI. My point is that the URI in that link (on which I clicked) is (e.g.) http://localhost:8080/rest/97/ec/60/bc/97ec60bc-65c4-46ba-9d09-91666574e1e4. How is that getting redirected to http://localhost:8080/rest/97/ec/60/bc/97ec60bc-65c4-46ba-9d09-91666574e1e4/fcr:metadata? That is what seems to me to be flatly wrong.

Here is the answer to "how" it is getting redirected:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-http-api/src/main/resources/views/common.js#L24
I understand none of that. Are you telling me that it has something to do with the JavaScript in the HTML? Why aren't we just using the right URI to begin with?

I am telling you that the JavaScript checks if the resource is a binary, and if that binary has a Link header of "describedby", and if so it redirects to that view.
What are you suggesting?

I do not understand your explanation. When I go to http://localhost:8080/rest/97/ec/60/bc/97ec60bc-65c4-46ba-9d09-91666574e1e4 there is no redirect, and when I go to http://localhost:8080/rest/97/ec/60/bc/97ec60bc-65c4-46ba-9d09-91666574e1e4/fcr:metadata there is no redirect. When does the redirect occur?
The redirect occurs when you navigate to the binary resource from somewhere else within the HTML UI.
Then why aren't we just using the correct URI to begin with in that link in HTML? Why are we putting in the wrong URI and then redirecting?
The navigation in the HTML UI is "follow-your-nose". We do not know the resource is a binary until it is actually requested.
Certainly we can. If we can do AJAX requests to get the type after the resource is requested, we can do them before to get its type.
Is there a reason to change the current approach?

I don't understand how it works or why it is there. If you do, and you think it is a good approach, then please supply a PR to #844 to reinstate it so that I can work on the weird jcr:content triple and we can get this done.

Andrew Woods I cannot duplicate the weird triple you saw or the blank screen. When I create a binary resource, I get the landing page you expect (the properties page) and when I look at the properties, I don't see the weird version triple you saw. I'm now using a rebased version of the PR (rebased after your fix for FCREPO-1649 Closed ). Can you check again and give me a really precise set of steps to follow to duplicate your results? (Ideally, I'd like to write an integration test against whatever weird failure is happening here, if it's still here...)
A. Soroka, please push your rebase commit so I can retest it.
Sorry!

Switch PRs to:

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/855

Here are the steps:

  • Go to the top of the code base
    • cd <whatever>/fcrepo4
  • Clear out existing data
    • rm -rf fcrepo4-data
  • Start fcrepo
    • mvn jetty:run -pl fcrepo-webapp
  • Go to the HTML UI, in browser
    • http://localhost:8080/rest/
  • Create a binary resource named "image"
    • Boom – no properties
That is not what I get after that series of steps. I get the props page (see attachment).

yes, but no props!

Do the same thing from a build of the master branch, and you will see props.

Oh, this is about what's in the props box? I took your remark "When creating a "binary" resource in the HTML UI, nothing is shown on the landing page." at face value.

I checked this with curl and http://localhost:8080/rest/image/fcr:metadata returns appropriate triples, so this is in the HTML/JS stuff, which means I'm off the ticket. I'm not prepared to debug JS. If you can verify the funky triple, I will try and track that down (I'm not seeing it in the RDF.)

To get the funky triple, perform the steps mentioned above to create the binary resource "image".
Then, create a version (v0) of that resource:
curl -i -XPOST -H"slug: v0" http://localhost:8080/rest/image/fcr:versions

When you perform a GET request on the "image".... funkadelic:
curl http://localhost:8080/rest/image/fcr:metadata
Okay, once again I will check it out at the top of the coming week.

The issue with the empty properties panel is here:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-http-api/src/main/resources/views/common.vsl#L9

The subject, $sub, is <resource>/fcr:metadata, we need to add some logic to instead find the triples of the NonRdfSource that is being described.
What is $helpers.getSortedTriples and what is $rdf.find?
This gives real impetus to FCREPO-1594 Closed .
